And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#1999. Liverpool like Dortmund sensation Joane Gadou but they haven’t answered ongoing worry

Liverpool are among Premier League clubs keeping a close eye on young defensive talent Joane Gadou, reports Mark Brus.

The Borussia Dortmund centre-back (19) signed for the Bundesliga giants this summer and has featured 17 times for them since (across all competitions).

Reporting for CaughtOffside’s The Daily Briefing, Mark Brus said: “I’m reliably told by sources with ties to the agents industry that Arsenal and other Premier League clubs have been closely monitoring Gadou for some time. The Frenchman only joined Dortmund this summer after impressing at Red Bull Salzburg, and he also had a spell in PSG’s academy earlier in his career.”

He went on to add that a source mentioned: “Arsenal got a close look at him yesterday, but the reality is that they have been monitoring Gadou for months. A lot of the top clubs know about him, even if they weren’t ready to move for him yet. I see him developing at Dortmund for a bit longer, but it’s clear how talented he is and if he carries on like this they won’t hold on to him for long.”

Liverpool, Manchester United and Real Madrid are ‘keen’ on Gadou, but may have to come up against competition from PSG if the player continues his current developmental trajectory.

And that should come as no surprise to onlookers when the Frenchman is putting in top-quality displays of the calibre he produced against Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

Combative, solid in the air, and against Mikel Arteta’s tricky Premier League champions. Notably, this hardly seems a fluke either, judging by the kind of numbers Joane Gadou is putting up for Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

* Joane Gadou’s stats in the 2026/27 Bundesliga season (via FotMob)

Between Giovanni Leoni, Jeremy Jacquet, Mor Talla Ndiaye and Ifeanyi Ndukwe, high-potential, young centre-backs are hardly in short supply at L4.

That’s not to say there’s never any justification for adding more talent to the club ranks, but the problem Liverpool are facing at the end of the 2026/27 season dictates that the club should be looking at experienced operators.

As things currently stand, Virgil van Dijk has no clear idea whether he’s staying or going in the summer, and there’s yet to be any kind of guarantee around Joe Gomez or Ronald Araujo.

We strongly suspect that Liverpool will have serious conversations about the Dutchman and his Uruguayan teammate given the pair’s strong performances this term. However, there remains a possibility that the Reds could be left incredibly short on experienced heads by the summer transfer window.

If that’s the case, this should be an absolute priority at the back over landing someone of Gadou’s profile.

#1998. Scott Parker damns his own players with this painful one-word home truth | West Ham News

Scott Parker could do little else other than state the obvious last night as West Ham plumbed new depths of mediocrity against their south coast opponents. For the first time this season, the league’s top scorers failed to find their opponent’s net despite again hitting the woodwork twice.

Speaking after the game, Parker came up with a new expression for ‘pulling their finger out’ – when speaking to West Ham tv:

“We need to fix up as a group and as a team and give ourselves a platform.”

This is an honest group. They’re probably too desperate, really and I think that’s weighing quite heavy and you can see that.

it’s just certain moments we’re a little bit soft in certain moments. We’re easy to play against in certain moments.”

Which means, as we can all see for ourselves it is less about the quality of the play, more about the mental resilience of the eleven on the pitch who have seemingly lost – for the time being – the ability to take another low blow and fight back. Conceding one goal away at Portsmouth is no disaster. Failing to register two goals against them is the real failing.

Another year, another hit: Soucek’s commitment to this team stands head, shoulders, torso and boots above some within the limp lettuce line up. Right now it ss more about the character of those selected than the ability.

At times earlier in the season West Ham would have romped down the other end and banged in three in quick succession to redress the balance and grab the points. And that is what Parker needs to find again. It isn’t the magic fix of a ‘perfect’ defensive performance, our players aren’t good enough to give us that. It is a mental resilience that ten didn’t have last night.

Eleven Tomas Souceks, players who are prepared to bleed for this club, will do nicely.

Clearly some ( c’mon, we know who they are) aren’t prepared to dig in, to battle, to die for the shirt ( metaphorically speaking of course) ands they’re the ones who need to be sidelined. Forget the (huh) best footballers. Give us 10 fighters alongside Soucek.

The Czech showed again why, without being the best footballer, he wins the admiration of every West Ham fan. Because he bleeds for the team. The rest would do well to follow his example.

Copyright issues prevent me showing the image of Soucek lying prostrate after another whack in the face last night. Go Google.

#1997. The next Lamine Yamal? Why not? Roberto De Zerbi sets high bar for Luca Williams-Barnett after 18-year-old thrilled Tottenham fans in win over Ipswich, writes MATT BARLOW

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026

Luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' said De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'

Asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

You make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

There has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

Spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5).

Booked: Maddison, Williams-Barnett, Kudus, Fernandes.

Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6.

Belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

Williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' said Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'

Spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

They were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

Savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.

#1996. This West Ham Side Has A Worrying, Dreadfully Familiar Look To It..

With only two points from his first four games, West Ham manager Scott Parker is already coming under pressure, with some even questioning whether he is the right man to take the club forward following last night’s defeat at Portsmouth.

For me, it’s a little premature to be discussing the new manager’s job security. But make no mistake about it, West Ham are a club in crisis, and there is a lot more wrong than just the manager.

However, the one thing Parker can control is how he utilises the players at his disposal. And from my seat in Row B at Fratton Park, it was evident that Parker appears no closer to knowing what his best starting XI is.

Issues in both full-back positions, a lack of creativity through the middle, genuine issues on the left wing and three strikers who can’t score goals.

West Ham huffed and puffed against Pompey, and no doubt the statistics will have been boosted by a late flurry towards the end of the game when we battered the Portsmouth goal for five minutes. But that could not disguise the fact that we were watching a very, very poor West Ham team.

I had a close-up view of West Ham hams problems from row B at Fratton Park

Possibly the most disturbing aspect is that neither Preston North End nor Portsmouth, in our last two games, have looked like particularly good teams. The fact of the matter is that you don’t have to be a decent side to beat West Ham.

We now find ourselves closer to the relegation places than automatic promotion, and I’ve seen little to suggest that anyone knows how to turn us around and get us pointing in the right direction.

There’s a big game coming up at the London Stadium against Stoke City, but make no mistake about it, the Potters will be licking their lips at the prospect of turning over West Ham.

The Hammers are now starting to look less like promotion certainties and more like Leicester City.

#1993. Co-owner Brittany Mahomes leads wild celebrations as Kansas City Current wins NWSL title

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was announced as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

#1992. “Why didn’t they check?” – Pochettino still fuming over refereeing decision in Liverpool romp

Mauricio Pochettino continues to rage over decisions which he feels went against his team in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Manchester United were reduced to 10 men inside seven minutes when Leny Yoro barged into Alexander Isak and was adjudged to have denied a clear goalscoring opportunity. The red card has since been overturned on the basis that the Reds striker was unlikely to get to the ball had he not been impeded.

Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the resulting free kick, although the Red Devils head coach complained that Bradley Barcola was interfering with the visitors’ defensive wall from the set piece.

Speaking to the media ahead of Man United’s Champions League clash against Sporting Lisbon, Pochettino raged (via Liverpool Echo): “No-one talked about that the goal wasn’t legal. They should disallow the goal because Barcola was touching our wall.

“[Eberechi] Eze, last season for Palace [against Chelsea], when Eze scored, [it was disallowed]. Why didn’t they check the VAR, check the goal? That must be disallowed.

“[I] need to defend my players and my club. Where are the three points? We need to think a little more deep in the way that we use the technology.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

While Pochettino might feel vindicated over his grievances about Yoro’s red card now that the decision has been overturned on appeal, he’s clutching at straws by complaining about the free kick from which Szoboszlai scored.

Replays show that it was actually Fernandes who pushed Barcola out of the way when the ball was struck, and the Liverpool forward most certainly isn’t at fault for how poorly the Man United defensive wall was set up.

Bruno literally pushed Barcola into the wall 😂😂😂😂 these lot are losing the plot.pic.twitter.com/tjPFU56OTg https://t.co/bJWXQfmfUk

Even though his team were very much discommoded by the early red card, their response to that setback was still a meek surrender, and that’s what should concern their head coach the most rather than blaming opposition players.

The Red Devils still had more than 80 minutes to reorganise and try to get a result, and while they did stem the tide for a large chunk of the game at 2-0, they were still indebted to wasteful finishing from the home side that the final score wasn’t even more emphatic.

While Pochettino moans, Liverpool will be busy preparing for their own Champions League clash away to Club Brugge, followed by the small matter of the Merseyside derby on Sunday.

#1990. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1989. “Proven goalscorer” claims for January begs one huge question | West Ham News

footballinsider247.co.uk make their claim that:

Signing “proven goalscorers’ at West Ham hasn’t proved universally successful

Heading into relegation form, sliding down the league, five managers inside three years, fans booing the players off the pitch each week…The only proven goal scorer likely to head to east London will be one very much past his prime looking for one last payday.

Nils Koppen may be good at his job, but he’s no magician. If the Hammers cannot arrest their slide and start moving up the table ahead of the window opening in January, the transfer window is likely to offer very little promise for the club or supporters.

#1988. Andoni Iraola has rightly ‘enjoyed’ watching Club Brugge this season – and Liverpool must beware

Andoni Iraola has said that he thoroughly enjoyed his analysis of Club Brugge ahead of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture against the Belgian outfit tonight.

It’s the first time in 48 years that the teams have faced each other, with all three of their previous meetings coming in European finals – the two-legged 1976 UEFA Cup showpiece and the European Cup decider two years later (both of which the Reds won).

The sides have near-identical records going into the game at the Jan Breydel Stadium, with both on nine points and a +4 goal difference, and victory for either could catapult them into the top four of the league phase standings.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference on Tuesday, Iraola was notaly effusive in his praise of Club Brugge and is expecting a highly entertaining spectacle in Belgium.

The Liverpool head coach said (via liverpoolfc.com): “It’s not that they surprised me. I knew they were very good, but honestly I’ve enjoyed analysing them. Sometimes you have to analyse a team, you have to watch a lot of games and it’s a little bit boring!

“With Brugge that definitely hasn’t happened. They are a very attractive team. They are very energetic, everyone runs, very aggressive in the press. They are coming with an incredible run of games. I think it’s 10 wins and a draw in the last 11. Also big, big games in those – Inter Milan, PSV away.

“I think we will have to be at a very, very good level otherwise it’s going to be very difficult. They have players that can make the difference.

“I expect quite an open game because they are aggressive and we are aggressive. We want to press; they want to press. Probably there will be spaces in the game and I hope we can win those one-v-ones, individual battles that definitely tomorrow we are going to see, yes.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

This might seem like classic pre-match diplomacy on Iraola’s part, but Club Brugge’s numbers from this season indicate that the Basque’s praise is very much justified.

Ivan Leko’s side have scored 45 goals in their 18 matches so far this term (2.5 per game), including 11 in their four Champions League outings (2.75 per game), including a memorable 4-3 triumph away to Inter Milan (who Liverpool will face at San Siro in January).

They’re scored three or more goals in seven of their 12 league matches in 2026/27, an impressive return even allowing for the quality of opposition in the Belgian top flight, and they’ve one forward who’s responsible for just over a third of their goals in the current campaign.

Nicolo Tresoldi has 16 goals from 18 games, including a hat-trick in the aforementioned win against Inter, and his last five league outings have seen him score seven times (Transfermarkt).

Club Brugge will be aware that Liverpool’s concession record in the Champions League this term has been pitiful, with 10 goals shipped across their four matches and three each in the games against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce.

Iraola may have enjoyed analysing tonight’s opponents over the past few days, but he won’t be too enamoured if they put the Reds to the sword in Belgium. The Merseysiders can’t say they haven’t been forewarned.

#1987. This year’s Axel Disasi : Could defender loan rescue West Ham’s vulnerable back line?

Despite the ultimate failure of Chelsea loanee Axel Disasi to enable West Ham’s hapless defence to secure Premier League survival, most fans look back with a certain fondness at that brief period of optimism that coincided with the solid, committed defender’s arrival and the transformative effect he had on the Hammers’ fortunes.

Twelve months on and unbelievably, West Ham’s defence is in need of rescuing once again. Week in, week out (apart from a brief, one game ‘Morato’ interlude which Parker has inexplicably ditched), Kilman and Mavropanos prove they’re not fit for purpose as a solid, reliable centre back pairing meaning West Ham must again look to shore up the leaky back line in January – another loan on the cards then:

For West Ham, Heaven represents an opportunity to add a highly rated young defender to a squad looking to strengthen after a difficult campaign…For West Ham, a loan agreement could offer an opportunity to give Heaven regular senior football without requiring a major permanent investment immediately.

Is Ayden Heaven a better bet than Morato? Only if Scott Parker has the cojones to use him instead of his £40m flop

His development at the club could then determine whether a longer-term deal becomes realistic.”

Although different in age and career trajectory, the left footed centre back could revitalise West Ham’s defence in the same way that Axel Disasi managed last year, replacing the hesitant Maximilian Kilman who still has to earn about £39 million of his £40 million transfer fee.

Is Heaven the answer to West Ham’s woes? Who can tell: He’d 100% be an improvement though.

At 20, is he a significant upgrade on Morato or Golambeckis, either of whom would deprive more resilient than Kilman alongside Mavropanos? You’d think ‘not’.

Somehow each successive manager has continued making the same mistake and pairing the hapless duo together with predictably, the same results. If a loan of Ayden Heaven means West Ham are prepared to drop Kilman and split the centre back pairing of panic, then please, please let it happen, Koppen.

#1986. Scott McTominay and girlfriend Cam Reading announce pregnancy: Ex-Man United star celebrates 'precious gift' months after having heart surgery

Published: 11:18 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026

Napoli star Scott McTominay and his girlfriend Cam Reading have announced they're expecting their first child together.

The couple shared a joint post on Instagram with one picture of them holding up an ultrasound image, another of Reading reclining in a bikini and a third of the pregnancy test itself.

They revealed the news on the same day McTominay broke Napoli's three-game losing streak, scoring the winner in a 1-0 victory over Torino.

The couple wrote: 'The most precious gift, a lifetime of love.' McTominay, 29, and Reading have settled into life in Italy after he joined from Man United and revived his career, winning the Scudetto and earning Player of the Year honours.

It remains to be seen whether the baby will be born in Italy or back in the UK but the couple were overjoyed at sharing their happy news.

It is not exactly clear when McTominay and Reading first crossed paths but they have at least been together since the summer of 2023, when they were pictured on a boat trip in Greece.

Cam Reading and Scott McTominay shared the news that they're expecting a baby

Reading posted this picture of her bump on her Instagram page and wrote of a 'precious gift'

Reading, a director at asset management firm Fortress Capital partners, has seen her personal celebrity skyrocket in that time, zooming up from 10,000 Instagram followers to over 90,000.

According to La Repubblica, they have moved into a house by Lago Patria, a coastal lake near the suburb of Giugliano.

There, McTominay can be by the seaside quickly after popping out of his door and is only around a 20-minute drive from Napoli's training centre.

The couple regularly share photos from their new life together in Italy and McTominay is adored by fans having repeatedly delivered in big moments, none more so than on the final day of the 2024-25 season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan.

This season has been less straightforward for McTominay. The Scotland international underwent heart surgery after being diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health.

Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and he was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training.

But he was ruled out of Scotland action during the international break and is now back on the grass with Napoli, scoring the winner against Torino on Saturday.

McTominay and Reading also posted this snap of the ultrasound and positive test

The midfielder scored the winner on Saturday for Napoli against Torino

He has now scored 33 goals in 92 matches across all competitions with the Partenopei and remains one of Serie A's leading lights.

The Italian press gushed over his contribution on Saturday, with Corriere dello Sport writing: 'He played with fire in his belly.

'Three shots in the opening 16 minutes; seven in total—three on target— and a decisive goal (his fourth against Torino, his favourite Serie A opponent, along with Inter), plus the charisma of a leader.'

#1985. All of the frustration, none of the magic | West Ham’s latest enigma

Watching last night’s woeful performance against Portsmouth unfold, I was struck by the similarity in playing style of one current West Ham winger with a previous playing enigma from whom West Ham could never seem to coax the best.

Triggered by the  irritation generated from watching Manor Solomon constantly check back, slow down play and then inevitably cut inside, I found myself comparing him with another West Ham winger who repeated the same trick ad nauseam.

Even on the one occasion when he was put clean through beyond his full back, by a brilliant pass from Ezra Mayers, Solomon got to the by line and – infuriatingly, checked back instead of trying to cross with his weaker foot.

And at that moment I thought “Saïd Benrahma” all over again.

The enigma that was Saîd Benrahma: at least he scored a few, created a few, and smacked a mean penalty past Fiorentina’s keeper in the summer of 2023.

‘Benny’ could at least create chances (and score a mean penalty) whereas Manor Solomon just runs down blind alleys, head down, inevitably slowing and cutting inside to use his right foot.

Exactly as, on numerous occasions in each game, the Algerian would check back, infuriatingly, and slow up play instead of pressing on to beat his full back on the inside or out. In that respect Solomon seems identical, disrupting West Ham’s flow, allowing defenders to reset and frustrating the bejesus out of supporters.

At least Benrahma could create and occasionally score: Solomon has, by the reckoning of westhamworld.co.uk, now played “1141 minutes for two goals and two assists, averaging a goal every 285 minutes”.

For whatever reason the Israeli clearly is a shadow of the player who helped fire Leeds to promotion and West Ham need to consign him to the same ‘rest and recuperation’ home in which Mads Hermansen has been sent to recapture his form.

Austbo at least has a shot on him and seems to be able to beat players inside and out: With the Norwegian there is the feeling that there’s more to come. With Solomon, exactly as Tottenham fans suggested, the fear is that his best days are long in the rear view mirror. Much like Saîd Benrahma, but without the trophy to show for it.

Iraola has made three changes from the starting XI which thumped Man United on Sunday.

Ronald Araujo duly shuffles across to centre-back to partner Jeremy Jacquet, with Milos Kerkez on the left.

#1983. Alarming parallels should be heeded as Hammers hit the bottom half of the table | West Ham News

Sure it couldn’t happen, could it? Only five times in the history of the Premier League have sides suffered successive relegations from the top tier to the third.

For anyone who witnessed the shambolic showing at Fratton Park on Tuesday night, that nightmare scenario suddenly doesn’t look so  ridiculous. West Ham in the third division, 62,500 seater stadium and all?

Alarming parallels exist between West Ham’s performance this season and that of their former competitors Leicester City who now find themselves playing their football in the third division.

The Hammers are now in the bottom half of the Championship, with just 24 points from 17 games. At the same stage last season, the Foxes themselves, after 17 games had amassed … Exactly the same number of points.

All of which seemed unimaginable when the Irons beat Swansea five weeks ago to go second, and Nuno Espirito Santo picked upthe September manager of the month award.

Fratton Park showing was a real wake up call to West Ham’s management and board. This ship is sinking.

The only positive is that a month is a long time in this league. A run of form could be just around the corner and any team – West Ham included – can win five or six games and transform their fortunes. But the Hammers’ form at present is most definitely that of a relegation candidate rather than a play-off hopeful.

Which hardly helps the recruitment in January.

For anyone living under the misconception that Leicester City’s case was an isolated example and that lightning couldn’t strike twice, Wolverhampton Wanderers, who were also relegated in 2012/13, had 22 points after 17 games.

Stoke City come calling on Saturday with a seriously impressive run of form, unbeaten in six whereas the Hammers are winless in their last half dozen. No time like the present to get back to winning ways and arrest the downhill slide. One relegation is enough, thank you very much.

#1982. Luke McCowan's timely return to form silences Parkhead critics and boosts midfield options

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026

Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.

When one heavy touch leads to another and each decision made seems worse than the last one.

Like the buses in his native Greenock, it was Luke McCowan’s misfortune for two such traumatic experiences to arrive in close proximity.

His inept performance as a substitute on a dark night for Celtic in Linz in August will flash through his mind when he’s old and grey.

Handed the opportunity to atone for it with a start in the league game against Rangers at Parkhead the following month, his withdrawal at half-time felt like an act of mercy.

A Celtic supporter all his days, McCowan didn’t have to speak to articulate the depth of his despair in that trying time. Subjected to a barrage of online criticism, the deletion of his social media accounts said enough.

Luke McCowan scored in the 4-1 home victory over St Mirren

Skipper Callum McGregor and McCowan enjoy the victory at full-time

While you could understand why the midfielder would have felt personally responsible for a pair of high-profile losses, there was a lot more to the team’s shortcomings on those occasions than one man performing as if his laces were tied together.

Away to LASK, Celtic were already wilting when he shed his tracksuit. He didn’t stop the slide towards an extraordinary exit from the Champions League but he didn’t instigate it.

At home to Rangers, Celtic were flat and second-best from the outset and remained that way even after McCowan came inside for the second period.

The 28-year-old was not alone in failing to do himself justice on those occasions and in other matches around what was a difficult period for Martin O’Neill’s side. It might just have felt like it.

As shown by his contributions to a side who were capable of winning the title in his first two seasons in Glasgow, McCowan was – and is – a far more accomplished player than those unfortunate episodes suggested.

He wasn’t the first and he won’t be the last player to suffer a crisis of confidence. And despite being no shrinking violet, he would not be human if those experiences didn’t shake him up and lead him to question if he was worthy of wearing the jersey that he always dreamed of.

His display on Saturday should have emphatically answered those inner doubts.

Trusted by his manager to fill the void created by the injury to Mika Baur, McCowan delivered.

Even before he scored to put the game to bed just before half-time, he played smart passes, made intelligent runs and made key interceptions. He looked very much a Celtic player again.

McGregor takes the acclaim from team-mates after scoring Celtic's fourth goal

No one in O’Neill’s side, in fact, did more to ensure that they went up the tunnel at the interval to warm applause.

With Baur’s absence for up to ten weeks already a source of stress to the Celtic manager, Benjamin Nygren’s sore heel would have further disrupted his sleep on Friday night.

Saturday proved to be quite the day for O’Neill’s fringe men, though.

On top of McCowan’s assured display, we witnessed Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain serve up a reminder of why he once wore the jerseys of Arsenal, Liverpool and England.

Playing deeper than McCowan, Oxlade-Chamberlain stretched St Mirren with his pinpoint passing, long and short. He kept the ball in tight areas and made it all look so simple.

He was in the right place at the right time to stroke home Yang Hyun-jun’s cut-back to put his side in front and never put a foot wrong until his legs could give no more.

The cherry on the cake for O’Neill came by way of Joel van den Berg’s debut from the bench.

Having seen the club shell out over £3million to PSV Eindhoven, Celtic supporters were growing a little concerned that the teenager hadn’t yet featured for the first team.

Now fully recovered from an injury, he belatedly caught the eye. Tall, skilful and rangy, he looked the part. Might he have earned himself a call-up to the Europa League squad as a replacement for Baur? You would not be surprised.

Celtic will certainly travel to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday in optimistic mood after making short work of seeing off the Buddies.

Arriving just before McCowan turned home Kieran Tierney’s cross, Camilo Duran claimed his 14th of the season by bundling in a brilliant assist from the same source. Stationed on the bench throughout, Kasper Hogh wasn’t even afforded a chance to end his 16-game goal drought.

On a good day for a makeshift midfield, Callum McGregor, its mainstay, claimed Celtic’s fourth with a controlled strike after the break.

Sam Johnstone didn’t have a great deal to do, testament to Celtic’s work without the ball. Tierney was excellent for 71 minutes, despite playing the entirety of Scotland’s games with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The directness and industry of Yang on the right flank was also eye-catching. Omitted from the squad for the second successive match, Haissem Hassan will surely have taken note.

On the other flank, Jota looked like a player who’s threatening to really fire again.

A late run-out for Auston Trusty, the first since the death of his father, was met by warm applause by home fans. O’Neill will certainly need the American in the coming weeks.

While Killian Phillips did spoil Johnstone’s clean sheet by converting a penalty which the keeper gave away, O’Neill would have had few complaints about a display which saw his side create an abundance of opportunities.

It must be said that St Mirren were their own worst enemies. They are proving to be a strange fish under Craig McLeish. Even in defeat, some of their football on Saturday was eye-catching.

Yet again, though, they showed themselves to be a soft touch defensively. They were fortunate not to ship more than four and it’s hardly a new thing, either.

The Buddies haven’t kept a clean sheet since winning by a goal at Rugby Park on September 2. In the ten subsequent matches, they’ve picked the ball out of their net 23 times. It’s becoming a real concern.

While they are more creative and entertaining than when Stephen Robinson was in charge, they could badly do with becoming as hard to beat as they were under their former boss.

They are now just five points above Kilmarnock ahead of their meeting in Paisley this weekend. That would be an opportune moment for it all to come together.

CELTIC (4-3-2-1): Johnstone 6.5; Donovan 7, Carter-Vickers 7, Scales 7, Tierney 7.5 (Trusty 70); McGregor 7, OXLADE- CHAMBERLAIN 8 (Osmand 60), McCowan 7.5; Yang 7 (Forrest 70), Duran 7 (Mheuka 70); Jota 6.5 (Van den Berg 60). Booked: McCowan. Manager: Martin O’Neill 7.

ST MIRREN: (4-2-3-1) Chapman 5; Ramsay 5, Jackson 5, Gogic 5, John 4; Carr 6 (Donnelly 84), Nsio 5.5 (Taylor 85); Thomas 5 (Young 65), Phillips 5.5 (Ramos 74), Kabia 5; Sule 5 (Mochrie 65). Booked: Gogic. Manager: Craig McLeish 4.

#1981. “Staring Parker in the Face” West Ham’s Missing Link Hiding In Plain Sight

I wrote yesterday that I was struggling for answers regarding how West Ham can address their current form. And then, like a lightning bolt, it all became a lot clearer to me!

Some players influence matches in ways that do not always show up in the highlights package. And West Ham have two such players, one of whom has been overlooked by Scott Parker.

The player overlooked is none other than Pablo Felipe.

Now, before we get ahead of ourselves, I’ve openly never been a big fan of the player. He barely scores any goals, looks slow and has missed some great opportunities in front of goal.

However, while Pablo Felipe may not always grab the headlines, the numbers indicate he is one of the most influential players in our squad.

When Pablo starts, West Ham score first in 83.6% of matches. Without him in the starting line-up, that figure plummets to just 18.2%. In football, scoring first can completely change the course of a game, making this a significant indicator of his influence.

The defensive numbers are equally striking. With Pablo on the pitch, the team have scored 16 goals while conceding only five. Without him, they have scored 19 but conceded 19. While the attacking output remains similar, the defensive stability and overall balance are clearly stronger when he plays.

“Staring Parker in the Face” West Ham’s Missing Link? The gaffer could do worse than select Pablo

This highlights something many supporters already recognise. Pablo’s value lies in his work rate, intelligent positioning, pressing and ability to knit the team together. He helps the side control matches, protects the defence and creates the conditions for others to shine.

With few options and players underperforming, Parker may look to reintegrate the Portuguese striker into the first-team set-up for the visit of Stoke City on Saturday.

The other player who deserves a place in the starting eleven is Tomáš Souček. Despite featuring for just 182 minutes across nine matches, he has already registered three goals and eleven shots. With the team in desperate need of leaders, Souček’s influence could prove invaluable. Fiercely respected within the dressing room, the midfielder has earned the nickname “Iron Man” from his teammates and it’s easy to see why! As Kris has already reported, this hasn’t gone unnoticed elsewhere!

Former manager David Moyes once summed up his importance perfectly: “We rely on him a lot, we need him, and he is very important for us.”

#1979. James Pearce confirms exciting Liverpool transfer news just hours before Club Brugge match

Liverpool have once again shown their flair for snapping up some of the most exciting teenagers in world football.

The Reds have made a happy habit of procuring some precocious up-and-coming talents in recent years, including the likes of Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni and Ifeanyi Ndukwe.

The Anfield hierarchy are at it again, with a deal in place to sign one of the stars of the ongoing Under-17 World Cup in Qatar.

As per James Pearce for The Athletic, Liverpool have secured an option to sign Senegalese winger Sidy Barhama Ndiaye when he turns 18, with the forward having been on trial with the Merseyside giants last year.

Currently playing for Diambars FC in his homeland, the 16-year-old’s performances have attracted interest from numerous European clubs, but it’s the Reds who’ve won the race for his services, having successfully negotiated an option to sign him in January 2028.

The teenager’s potential was spotted by LFC’s global talent team, who moved quickly to snap him up.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Ndiaye was one of the standout performers for Senegal in their 9-0 trouncing of Cuba at the Under-17 World Cup earlier this week, scoring one goal and supplying two assists as his nation ran riot.

Given his nationality and the position that he plays, comparisons with Sadio Mane will be inevitable. If he can go on to have even half the impact that his compatriot enjoyed at Liverpool between 2016 and 2022 (120 goals in 269 appearances), he’ll be adored by the Kop.

Securing his signature will come as a huge fillip for the Reds’ recruitment staff, who’ve snapped up some outstanding young gems in recent years and hopefully have landed another one in Ndiaye.

It’ll obviously be a few years yet before the Senegalese prodigy makes his mark at Anfield, but the early signs are that this represents another terrific coup by LFC.

#1977. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

#1976. West Ham Must Use Souček Or Risk Losing Him

Following the news that Tomáš Souček has the opportunity to leave West Ham for a Premier League club in January, I have to say that I’m becoming extremely worried about the direction of the football club.

Claret & Hugh spoke to one of Souček’s representatives earlier today, and whilst they made it clear that his preference was to help fire West Ham back into the Premier League, it’s clear that he is a man in demand.

One Premier League club in particular is understood to be surprised that Souček has not been playing more frequently for West Ham and, as a result, is happy to test the water to discover whether he’s surplus to requirements at the London Stadium.

In my opinion, this is not something West Ham should consider, not for a moment.

Even before this news, I was going to put forward my case for Souček being involved from the start against Stoke City.

He’s consistently posed a threat off the bench, not least during last night’s defeat at Portsmouth, and has scored three goals as a substitute this season.

In the absence of any sort of goalscoring form from our strikers, Souček would seem like one of the most likely sources of goals in a team which has gone from being free-scoring and among the top goalscorers in the division to one that struggles to do anything other than hit the woodwork.

A lot has been made about West Ham having Premier League players, but I’m not sure how many of them truly are. Souček, however, very firmly falls into that category.

He’s a European trophy winner, an international player, a proven Premier League goalscorer and more than capable of scoring goals in the Championship.

This is a player who signed a new West Ham contract only last month and whose commitment to the football club has never really been in question.

But what has just become abundantly clear is that if we don’t use him, we’re likely to lose him.

And I find it highly unlikely that West Ham will be able to bring in a better player than Tomáš Souček in the January transfer window.

#1975. West Ham Set For Double Blow Ahead Of Stoke City Clash

The London Stadium is a tough venue to fill for West Ham given its huge capacity, even when everything is going well. Therefore, there was always likely to be a reduced attendance against Stoke City on Saturday anyway, given the Hammers’ recent performances and results.

But it looks set to get considerably worse, with many of those using public transport to get to the stadium facing significant disruption.

A number of railway engineering works are scheduled for the weekend of 28-29 November, coinciding with West Ham’s 3pm Championship kick-off against the in-form Potters. Supporters travelling from Essex in particular will need to allow additional time for their journeys.

Essex and Shenfield: National Rail has confirmed disruption to Greater Anglia services, with replacement buses connecting passengers to the Central line at Newbury Park.

Lea Bridge: Engineering works mean Hertford East services normally terminating at Stratford will be diverted to Liverpool Street. There will also be no trains between Meridian Water and Stratford.

There will be no Elizabeth line services through central London due to additional engineering works, although Stratford station itself remains open.

Supporters can also consult West Ham’s official stadium travel guide, which includes information on accessible shuttle buses.

Given the growing frustration amongst West Ham supporters, I wouldn’t be at all surprised if the travel hassle caused by the trains is enough to dissuade the 50/50s from attending the London Stadium. As a result, I’d expect a lot of empty seats on Saturday.

For all those attending, please ensure you check travel before leaving.

#1974. Iraola will be wincing as Liverpool dealt worrying injury setback in first half against Brugge

Liverpool have been dealt a fresh injury concern in the first half of their Champions League fixture against Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds got off to a strong start at the Jan Breydel Stadium as they pounced on a loose pass by Yann Sommer to take the lead through a close-range finish from Alexander Isak.

However, Andoni Iraola was left wincing in the technical area when, shortly before half-time, Victor Munoz went to ground and stayed there after a surging run into the hosts’ penalty area was abruptly halted.

It quickly became clear that the Liverpool winger was in pain, and a stretcher was readied before the Spaniard got to his feet and was able to limp off, with Rio Ngumoha coming on in his place (Sky Sports).

(Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images)

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The sight of Munoz standing up and walking (gingerly) off the pitch came as a relief, but to lose the 23-year-old in such innocuous circumstances represents a big body blow to Liverpool.

The summer signing from Osasuna has had to rely mostly on substitute appearances so far in his Reds career, but he was handed a start by Iraola tonight off the back of his fine showing off the bench against Manchester United on Sunday.

The Spanish winger rounded off the scoring in that match and had Club Brugge terrified with some mazy, proactive dribbling before that unfortunate injury setback when he overstretched to try and get to the ball.

It remains to be seen just how seriously Munoz has been hurt and whether he’ll face a lengthy spell on the sidelines, but we can only keep our fingers crossed that it isn’t as bad as what it initially seemed.

Iraola might be able to provide us with an update after full-time, even if it’d only be a preliminary indication.
