#1941. THE END GAME? Writing is on the wall for McCann after revitalised Dons ran riot at Rugby Park

Published: 18:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:11 EST, 22 November 2026

Let’s face it, Neil McCann was never the most popular of appointments with Kilmarnock fans, but not even his harshest critics could deny that he did a fine job in keeping the club in Scotland’s top flight last season.

Unfortunately for him, it looks increasingly likely that he isn’t going to get the chance to repeat the trick this time around.

The writing already appears to be on the wall for the 52-year-old. A question of when, rather than if, he is given his jotters.

By all accounts, he hasn’t lost the dressing room. Which is just as well, because he has well and truly lost the punters, whose collective mood shifted from angry to apathetic over the course of 90-odd thoroughly entertaining minutes at Rugby Park on Saturday.

McCann knows this himself. It is not as if he is operating with the blinkers on.

It's a tough watch for Neil McCann as his Kilmarnock team go down 4-2 to Aberdeen

His assessment of his team’s performances week-to-week tends to be pretty honest, as it was again this weekend.

The problem is, as he put it, that he is coming across ‘like a broken record’.

His team are hopeless at the back and toothless up top, with some encouraging stuff in between. If the supporters are sick of hearing it, imagine how scunnered McCann must feel saying it. He certainly looks it.

If they continue to defend like this, relegation is a nailed-on certainty.

They shipped four here — and it could have very easily been a few more — to take their tally to 33 conceded for the season in just 14 games. It’s laughable, there’s no other way to dress it up.

Aberdeen’s Kevin Nisbet scored twice in four first-half minutes, capitalising on a woeful clearance from keeper Nico Mantl to put the Dons ahead, before curling a free-kick straight through the weakest wall you’ve ever seen in your life to double the visitors’ advantage.

New Dons boss Mario Frick can't hide his delight after victory in first game in charge

The third goal — shortly after Greg Kiltie had given McCann’s men a lifeline — was the worst of the lot. Former Rugby Park skipper Brad Lyons ghosted in behind the completely unaware Michael Schjonning-Larsen to head the ball home after Cathal McCarthy failed to stop Nesta Guinness-Walker’s cross from the left touchline.

Shocking stuff all round, and exactly the type of goal which has killed Killie all season — and will continue to do so until something drastic changes.

Let’s not forget, the recent international break afforded McCann and his staff a fortnight to work on things on the training pitch ahead of what is going to be a gruelling winter schedule.

While the Killie manager will ultimately be the one to pay the price, his players need to have a right good look at themselves too. There was simply no sign of anyone in that backline taking any sort of responsibility.

Kilmarnock’s next three games are against St Mirren, Hibernian and Motherwell — the three sides currently directly above them in the table.

An absolute minimum of four points from that run is required, otherwise this is going to get rather ugly. In truth, defeat in Paisley this weekend may well be the final nail in McCann’s coffin.

On the other hand, things are finally starting to look up for the Dons.

New manager Mario Frick has promised to bring heavy metal football to these shores, and if Saturday is anything to go by, the ex-Liechtenstein international is a man of his word.

McCann's job looks to be on the line after bottom club Killie succumbed to another defeat

His team were a joy to watch going forward here, particularly in the first half.

It was a million miles away from the kind of turgid football offered up under his predecessor as Dons manager, Stephen Robinson.

Speed, intensity, aggression, quality. The performance was full of it.

You could count the number of times the Dons faffed about with the ball on one hand. Every time there was an opportunity to get forward, they took it.

Ante Palaversa, making his first appearance of the campaign, was at the heart of it.

For whatever reason, Robinson never fancied the Croatian, a stance which perplexed the Pittodrie faithful. Indeed, the 26-year-old — once on the books of Manchester City — was deemed surplus to requirements over the summer.

The Dons will be delighted there were no takers.

He was outstanding here as he commanded that space between midfield and defence without breaking sweat. Nobody in Killie colours could get near him.

Both Nicky Devlin and Guinness-Walker bombed up their respective wings all day, while some of the link-up play between Nisbet — who should have had a hat-trick before Findlay Marshall wrapped things up late on — and Hicham Mahou was delightful.

Defensively, they were all over the shop at times, and no doubt they will be punished heavily at Ibrox on Tuesday night if they are as open as this.

But this was a display to simply be enjoyed rather than picked apart. It makes a change.

KILMARNOCK (4-2-3-1): Mantl 3; McCarthy 4, Kamson-Kamara 3 (Brandon 46), Stanger 4, Schjonning-Larsen 4; Lowery 6, Tshibola 5 (McKenzie 85); Ring 3 (O’Hara 46), Kiltie 6 (Clescenco 83), Hugill 5.5; Owen 4 (John-Jules 54). Booked: Owen, Hugill. Manager: Neil McCann 3.

ABERDEEN (4-1-3-2): Muller 5; Devlin 6, Molloy 6, Milne 6, Guinness- Walker 7; PALAVERSA 8 (Aremu 61); Lyons 7, Briedl 7 (Mouloula 61), Armstrong 6.5 (Marshall 71); Mahou 6 (Smith 80), Nisbet 8. Booked: None. Manager: Mario Frick 7.

#1937. AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Counter-attacking clinic sees Rossoneri run riot

AC Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four.

It was a game that promised entertainment from the early stages, and Milan took command thanks to an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani and a much-needed goal from Goncalo Ramos, before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri ran away with things in the second half, with Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse netting off the bench before Christian Pulisic got a goal of his own to add some gloss to the scoreline. There were chances to make it an even bigger margin, but five would have to do.

Given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus had all won prior to kick-off, it was important that Milan matched their results to keep up the pressure at the top end of the table, and they did so in emphatic fashion.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Frosinone started the game better and called Mike Maignan into action inside the first minute with a close-range header that was saved, though the flag was up. Then, a deflected strike from Masini on the edge of the box ended up scraping the upright and going behind for a corner.

However, it was Milan who struck first at San Siro. Luka Modric deserves the plaudits for an outstanding through ball to find Adrien Rabiot’s run in behind, and the Frenchman’s square pass was heading towards Christian Pulisic’s run but was turned into his own net by Calvani, leaving Palmisani rooted.

The frantic pace of the early stages continued, as a lovely exchange between Diego Moreira and Pulisic saw a threatening cross turned behind. A few minutes later, Yunus Musah found Moreira who had a shot deflected for a corner, which Goncalo Ramos rose and met well but headed over the bar.

Frosinone kept providing reminders that they too pose a threat going forward, such as on the quarter-hour mark when Kvernadze surged down the left and got off a low shot from a narrow angle that Maignan had to parry behind. The corner wasn’t properly dealt with, and Cittadini flashed one across the six-yard box that Rabiot had to put into the stands.

Just like with the first goal, Milan punished Frosinone for not making the most of their spell of pressure. Goncalo Ramos was the man who started and finished a flowing counter-attack, robbing Calvani of possession before running towards goal. Musah’s through ball was run onto by the electric Moreira, who found Rabiot, and the Frenchman’s cut-back was tucked away by the Portuguese.

The two-goal lead was very quickly halved though, as Frosinone got the goal their pressure had threatened. Kvernadze’s run down the left and cut-back from the byline was scuffed onwards by Ghedjemis into the path of Masini, who toe-poked it in at the far post.

In the 34th minute, there was a moment that enraged the Milan players, staff and fans. The referee blew his whistle for a shirt pull on Rabiot just as Milan went through on goal with two men in behind and just the goalkeeper to beat. The official apologised, but it felt like a certain goal had been taken away.

It was a half played at a hundred miles an hour, and it ended that way too. Pulisic flashed an effort over the bar from a good position, while Davide Bartesaghi’s low cross towards Ramos was cut out in the nick of time as Milan continued to get joy down the flanks.

Amorim opted to make an intriguing change at half-time, bringing off Bartesaghi and replacing him with Ardon Jashari. This change in turn saw Musah shift to left-back, a role that he played against Genoa in the last match, and from minute one.

The change proved to be an absolute masterstroke, as Jashari scored inside three minutes. A ball was sent long to Ramos who knocked it down to Rabiot, whose first touch was a lovely through ball to the Swiss midfield. It looked like he had overrun it with the square option not used, but he lashed a shot in at the near post.

Not long after the goal, Ramos gestured towards the bench that he felt some discomfort. He wanted to play through it but Amorim took no risks, opting to bring Alphadjo Cisse on to lead the line.

There was a rather rare occurrence in the 54th minute, as Milan were awarded an indirect free-kick after Palmisani picked up a back pass from Calvani. Modric laid it off to Rabiot, but the goalkeeper made up for his error with a good save.

Continuing the trend of impact substitutions, Cisse got his ninth goal of the season right on the hour mark. A Frosinone corner was cleared and Pulisic found Moreira who had the Italian for company, and he finished the through ball by the Belgian past Palmisani with his trademark composure. The offside flag went up, but after a long check the goal was given.

Milan continued to look like scoring every time they got out of their own half, and Pulisic joined the fun in the 68th minute with a goal of his own. Frosinone again left one man back for a corner that was cleared, allowing the American to easily outpace Terzic with a run from inside his own half, dinking over Palmisani to make it 5-1.

With 20 minutes left on the clock, Amorim brought Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan on for Diawara and Musah. The final change saw Omari Hutchinson replace Pulisic.

Pavlovic looked far from 100% when he came on, appearing dizzy at certain moments. The head coach seemed to suggest coming off so as not to risk things, but he played on.

Milan had chances to make the scoreline even more impressive, with Moreira and Hutchinson squandering a couple of chances on the break. However, at full-time the team were rightly applauded by the San Siro crowd.

#1930. Player Ratings: AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone – Rabiot unstoppable; super attack

AC Milan clinched a comfortable win against Frosinone and individual brilliance certainly had a hand in that. Below are the player ratings for the Rossoneri.

Ahead of what will be a busy month, Milan knew that a win tonight would do them a lot of good, so that’s exactly what they managed to achieve. Goals from Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic set them up nicely, as well as an early own-goal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Rabiot (8 – MOTM): He just can’t help himself from getting goal contributions! Two more assists today, three if you count the own-goal, and his running is becoming a proper weapon for Milan. He’s just unstoppable when he gets going.

👔 Amorim (7.5): I think this was more or less a home run tactically. Frosinone were always going to try to have a high line, so the head coach exploited that with the help of Rabiot and the passing abilities of his teammates. Benching Cisse was bold, but it turned out to be just the right move.

Maignan (6): I’m not sure he could have done better on the goal, as it was really hard to predict where the cross would end up. Anyway, he made a couple of decent stops and was good with his feet, even if there was a scare in the first half.

Gila (6.5): Let me just say straight off the bat that he wasn’t far away from a 7. However, I think he could have done better to stop the cross on the goal conceded, and he had a few really poor passes as well. On the plus side, he was decent in possession overall and had a key clearance in the second half.

De Winter (6.5): He continues to marshal the defence well, though he lacked concentration on a few occasions today. It didn’t prove to be costly and similarly to Gila, there was definitely more good than harm, but the rating is affected a tad.

Diawara (6.5): I don’t think he could have got to the ball quicker on the goal, not to mention that it’s hard to anticipate such a deflection. As far as I’m concerned, it was solid defending from him, including some nice clearances to stop a few dangerous crosses.

Bartesaghi (6): Defensively he did okay, which was all that was required of him, but the main contributions were in attack. I think we saw some really good runs forward from him, although the crosses had mixed results. It seems fair with a 6 for him.

Moreira (7.5): His run before the second goal was crucial, of course, and he also managed to get an assist (good pass in the end, as VAR confirmed). For a higher rating, I would have liked to see more sharpness in the final third, as he had a couple of very good shooting opportunities that he missed.

Modric (8): My word, the pass before the first goal was just magnificent! That alone shows just how much he means to this team, but he also continued to do well with his passing and movement after that. For me, the rating does deserve to be that high, but maybe I’m blinded by the aforementioned pass.

Musah (7): He did really well to unleash Moreira just before the second goal, playing it perfectly. On the goal conceded, it was just unlucky in my opinion, he did everything right by getting a toe on it. The block at the start of the second half was just brilliant too, showcasing good defensive skills.

Pulisic (7.5): Amorim always says he lets the pitch do the talking and that was the case today. He wasn’t flashy by any means, but did very good work in silence (such as the movement before the own-goal) and was eventually rewarded with the goal. Stunning finish by the way. An 8 perhaps?

Rabiot (8 – MOTM): He just can’t help himself from getting goal contributions! Two more assists today, three if you count the own-goal, and his running is becoming a proper weapon for Milan. He’s just unstoppable when he gets going.

Ramos (7.5): Finally, back on target! Overall, it was a very encouraging one for him as the goal was the result of great positioning and hard work, which helped on the other goals too (opening up space). He could have had a second too if he hadn’t been stopped by the referee.

Jashari (7): That’s one way to make an impact! The finish was fantastic and really surprised the goalkeeper. He had a few more good runs after that, so this was definitely a performance that he can build on.

Cisse (7): It was an easy finish on the goal, it has to be said, but he still timed the run very well. He also showed off some good understanding in the centre-forward, which was nice to see. It wasn’t nice to see the unnecessary yellow card at the end, though.

Pavlovic (N/A): I didn’t see enough to give him a rating.

Estupinan (N/A): I didn’t see enough to give him a rating.

Hutchinson (N/A): I didn’t see enough to give him a rating.

Amorim (7.5): I think this was more or less a home run tactically. Frosinone were always going to try to have a high line, so the head coach exploited that with the help of Rabiot and the passing abilities of his teammates. Benching Cisse was bold, but it turned out to be just the right move.

Exactly. If Estupinan had given that performance he would have gotten a 5 rating on here. Bartesaghi is not any better defensively. Maybe a little better going forward.

Was a good game overall. Frosinone is similar to us in many ways, one major being they like to attack. They do however ship goals and it showed tonight. They’re a good team though as they were only 4 points behind us heading in the round, so they weren’t as easy a team as people are making out here. I hope we can build on these sort of performances. It’s very easy on the eyes, however when we lose it’s quite telling. And when things don’t click we really struggle. All in all though we’re doing well despite many things. Great strike by Jashari and Puli n Moreira causing huge problems as per usual. Happy for Ramos for the goal, hopefully that unlocks him but he did have some moments in the game where he could have done better. And then 20 year old Cisse comes on …. Anyways. On to the next one. Good work…

#1929. Mauricio Pochettino was immediately up against it in his first few days at this slow-motion car crash of a club - Man United's 4-0 loss at Liverpool showed how much he has to do: OLIVER HOLT

Published: 14:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 20:01 EST, 22 November 2026

A drone spied on his first training session, his star striker stayed up into the early hours obsessing over Grand Theft Auto the day he arrived, his best player has paused contract talks, his chief executive praised the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and the club banned four supporters for three years for throwing a tennis ball on to the pitch.

That was before the football started. And the fates had decreed that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge as head coach of this misused, abused, diminished, fallen slow-motion car crash of a football club that was once Manchester United but which has lost all sense of its place in the modern football firmament was to be away to Liverpool at Anfield.

And then Pochettino picked a centre-half, Matthijs de Ligt, who had not started a Premier League game for more than a year. And De Ligt began the game by watching a long ball sail over his head as if it were a rare curiosity to be observed rather than to be dealt with and before you could blink, Leny Yoro had been sent off trying to clear up De Ligt’s mess.

So at least Pochettino got to see United set a new record. Yoro was sent off after seven minutes and 23 seconds and that has never been done more quickly by United in the league. So there was that. De Ligt went on, it is sad to report, to have such a dreadful game that it was tempting to watch it through your fingers. Not the best selection decision by the new boss.

And in the stands, Omar Berrada, the strangely bullish United chief executive, looked colder and colder and more and more pale in the chill and, beside him, Jason Wilcox, the director of football, slid deeper and deeper into his big coat until he nearly disappeared from view. Which, presumably, was what he was hoping to do.

Mauricio Pochettino was given a near-impossible task in his first game as manager of Manchester United

Leny Yoro (right) was sent off just minutes into their 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool at Anfield

The Reds dominated from then on, with teenage winger Rio Ngumoha one of the Reds' stars

And in the row behind them, Sir Alex Ferguson gazed down on what remained of the great club he had built. James Nesbitt, the esteemed actor who is Ferguson’s friend, sat next to him in the directors’ box. One of Nesbitt’s best performances was in The Missing. The United defence were starring in the remake.

And the Liverpool fans loved it. ‘You’re going down with the City,’ they sang at the United fans. ‘You’re getting sacked in the morning,’ they sang at Pochettino, as he stood, arms tightly folded on the touchline. When it got to 4-0, the Kop broke out another ditty. ‘Poch is at the wheel,’ they sang over and over again.

So, welcome to Manchester, Mauricio. Welcome to the sight of United consolidating their position one off the bottom of the Premier League. If they keep this going for another week, they will be in the bottom three of the top flight in December for the first time in more than 50 years. If Pochettino did not know it before, he knows it now: there is an awful lot of saving to be done on the red side of Manchester.

This is a relegation fight that United are in. Don’t kid yourself that it’s not. The last time they dropped out of the top flight in 1973-74, they won three games in their first 11 matches. This season, they have won just once in the first 11 and that was at home to Ipswich Town on August 30th. A lot of the teams around them have got something about them, too. They certainly have more spirit than this rabble.

In that context, it was not the best omen that this was the worst result in a United manager’s first game for more than 100 years. If Pochettino thought getting the USA to win the World Cup was a big ask, rebuilding United is up there with it. This is a club mired in dysfunction on and off the pitch. It is a Herculean task to rescue them and we are about to find out whether Pochettino has it in him.

It was strange seeing a new United manager anointed at Anfield as the crowd sang You’ll Never Walk Alone and the Kop flew its flags and the faces of Shankly, Paisley, Dalglish, Klopp and the rest stared down from the banner of all the bosses here who have won league titles. Pochettino stood on the sideline and drank it all in, right until kick off.

It was his misfortune that this is also a Liverpool team beginning to click. Florian Wirtz is beginning to express himself and that is a wonderful sight. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak are becoming a formidable partnership. Rio Ngumoha scared Diogo Dalot rigid. Liverpool are rising again as United flounder.

It did not take long for Pochettino to get his first look at the uselessness that has afflicted United for most of this season. Only seven minutes had gone when Ronald Araujo drove a searching ball over the top of the United defence. De Ligt watched it go and abrogated responsibility for it, expecting Yoro to cover. Isak sprinted after it and by the time Yoro finally reacted, it was too late. Isak was on to it.

Pochettino opted to start Matthijs de Ligt (right) - but he struggled throughout the game

He knows the size of the task of saving United - and whether he can do it will determine his legacy as a manager

Liverpool, meanwhile, are starting to click - and Florian Wirtz is at the centre of that rise

Isak got ahead of Yoro and pushed the ball forwards. It was a heavy touch and would have run on to Lammens but Yoro compounded his error by bundling Isak down on the edge of the area. He was sent off by referee Sam Barrott. Only seven minutes and 23secs had elapsed. It was the quickest sending off in United’s Premier League history. It was not a controversy. It was just a show of defensive incompetence.

A free-kick in that kind of position might as well be a penalty when Dominik Szoboszlai is standing over it. He lashed it low and hard past the edge of the United wall. Bruno Fernandes shook a half-interested leg at it. It whistled past him and bulged the corner of the United net.

Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Araujo (Gomez 85), Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez; Szoboszlai, Mac Allister (Nyoni 72); Barcola (Munoz 72), Wirtz, Ngumoha (Frimpong 78); Isak (Koumas 85)

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Tsimikas, McConnell, Chiesa

Goals: Szoboszlai 10, Wirtz 13, Ngumoha 66, Munoz 82

Man United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, De Ligt, Martinez; Tielemans (Mount 65), Mainoo (Santos 87); Mbeumo (Maguire 22), Fernandes, Dorgu (Mazraoui 65); Cunha (Zirkzee 46)

Subs not used: Heaton, Heaven, Diallo, Lacey

Three minutes later, Liverpool were further ahead. Ngumoha embarrassed Dalot down the Liverpool left – not for the last time – and pulled a cross back for Wirtz. It was just behind the Germany playmaker but Wirtz has beautiful technique and somehow, he hooked it goalwards with his left foot and it crashed in off the underside of the bar.

United were in chaos. Pochettino looked stunned. He brought on Harry Maguire for Grand Theft Auto aficionado Bryan Mbeumo after 22 minutes. Maybe it was a bitter pill for Mbeumo. Maybe it will have just allowed him to spend more time with his PlayStation. Practice makes perfect, after all.

And so United spent the rest of the half repelling a siege of their goal. Fernandes summoned one shot on target but it dribbled apologetically through to Alisson from the edge of the area. Most of the time, though, it was like the Alamo at the United end. Maguire made one particularly heroic block from Isak.

Liverpool should have gone three-nil up just before the hour. Wirtz played a fine through ball to Barcola, who ran clear of the defence. Barcola had only Lammens to beat but instead of slotting the ball past him, he tried to dribble around him, got his feet mixed up and kicked the ball out of play.

There was frustration at Anfield. They wanted more than this. This was a chance to rub United’s noses in it, to inflict more misery on their hapless rivals. And yet, there was a sense they were letting them off the hook.

That feeling deepened when De Ligt made a dreadful mess of intercepting a lofted pass to Isak, missed his kick and fell over. Isak raced through but then blasted his shot hopelessly high and wide. Then Barcola turned De Ligt and hit another shot too high.

Liverpool could not keep missing all afternoon, though, and they finally got their third when Barcola skipped past Lisandro Martinez on the halfway line as if he wasn’t there and sprinted down the right. He squared the ball across the box to Ngumoha and Ngumoha slammed it unerringly past Lammens. Victor Munoz drilled home the fourth eight minutes from time and United’s humiliation was complete.

#1928. "It's like Zidane" - Spanish media in awe of "devastating" Jude Bellingham after Real Madrid win

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:10

Real Madrid produced a sensational second-half comeback to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday evening, with England star Jude Bellingham proving instrumental after being introduced at half-time.

Jose Mourinho's side were trailing 1-0 at the interval following Ivan Perisic's penalty, but Federico Valverde restored parity before the 23-year-old produced a spectacular volley to put Los Blancos ahead. Kylian Mbappe scored twice, and Vinicius Junior added a fifth to complete the turnaround.

Bellingham's influence attracted widespread praise from the Spanish media, with several publications describing him as the decisive figure in Madrid's transformation.

His 45-minute contribution included a goal, an assist and a series of impressive individual statistics.

AS were particularly impressed, publishing the headline "Bellingham: lo cambio todo" - 'Bellingham changed everything'.

Manu de Juan highlighted how the England international reorganised Madrid's midfield, allowing Arda Guler to operate deeper and giving the hosts greater control and attacking momentum. AS also praised his spectacular volley for the 2-1 lead and his subsequent assist for Vinicius.

El Pais delivered perhaps the most glowing assessment, publishing the headline "El esplendor deslumbrante de Bellingham impulsa la goleada del Madrid al PSV" - Bellingham's 'dazzling brilliance' drives Madrid's thrashing of PSV.

David Alvarez argued that Madrid's first-half performance had been lifeless and directionless, with Bellingham's introduction restoring clarity, composure and quality. His spectacular volley was described as a beautiful and devastating goal, with the newspaper suggesting the Englishman's arrival completely transformed the contest.

Mundo Deportivo labelled Bellingham a "superestrella" - 'superstar' - and suggested that he is currently Madrid's best player, while highlighting how his introduction changed the game.

ElDesmarque were equally enthusiastic, awarding the midfielder 9/10 and naming him their MVP. They highlighted his immediate influence, spectacular goal and assist for Vinicius, describing his 45 minutes as an outstanding exhibition.

Real Madrid-focused publications Defensa Central and madridistaReal went even further, awarding him 10/10 and 9.5/10 respectively. Both considered his introduction the turning point in Madrid's victory.

Spanish radio station Cadena SER also marvelled at his volley, with several commentators comparing the technical brilliance of the finish to something Zinedine Zidane might have produced - 'It's like Zizou,' one remarked.

Mourinho was equally impressed, describing the England international's performance as "absolutamente devastador" - 'absolutely devastating'.

The Portuguese coach explained that he had initially considered leaving Bellingham out to protect him from fatigue, believing Madrid could win without him. However, he admitted that having the midfielder available from the bench proved decisive.

Mourinho also described Bellingham as a different type of player who provided something Madrid had been missing during the opening 45 minutes.

The statistics underline why the praise was justified. Despite playing just 45 minutes, Bellingham registered one goal, one assist and created three chances. According to Sofascore, he also completed 100% of his attempted dribbles, won all of his tackles and claimed 75% of his duels.

His influence extended beyond the spectacular finish, with his movement between the lines helping Madrid establish control and create opportunities for their forwards.

There is little doubt that Bellingham was the defining figure in Madrid's comeback - while Mourinho's triple half-time substitution and improved collective pressing also played important roles, the Englishman's ability to bring structure, energy and creativity to the midfield was particularly striking.

Receiving such glowing praise from the Spanish media and his manager after just 45 minutes illustrates the level Bellingham can reach when operating at his best. His goal may have been the highlight, but it was his all-round contribution that made this one of his most impressive performances of the season.

#1927. Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Defensive rebuilding is next summer’s big project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

United were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

“There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick said. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”

There was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

He recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

Asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He showed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

“There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”

Speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

“But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ

The hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

“Scoring before half-time is always important if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV

Dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

Man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

The Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

Mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

The Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb

What a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

Wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

Some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you…

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa

Enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

We are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

Ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

End-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ

There will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

You would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

And United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

What a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

Davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

There’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second big save from Lammens. United look a threat going forward but then so do Ipswich, who are picking their moments to break and doing so well.

Rashford tries his luck from long range with a knuckle-ball free-kick. He doesn’t get any accuracy on the strike and it harmlessly flies off target.

This game has exploded into life in the last couple of minutes. End to end action. Scherpen first denying Dalot, then Ipswich going straight down the other end from a long punted clearance and Enciso, holding off Shaw and Mbeumo, forcing a save from Lammens. In keeping with the basketball nature of things, United then went back up the other end, with Cunha overhitting a cross for the onrushing Rashford before Fernandes’ goalbound shot is blocked. It’s certainly entertaining.

Chances at both ends! Firstly, Emersonn hacks Man Utd’s corner away, and Enciso uses his blistering speed to outpace Shaw and Mbeumo, creating a one-on-one with Lammens, who does excellently to smother the shot. Then Man Utd then fly forward straight away and Cunha fires a low delivery across the six-yard box which is marginally out of Rashford’s reach.

Man Utd counter as Fernandes releases Mbeumo with a ball over the top. The hosts recycle the ball well after Rashford crosses, allowing Dalot to cut in or his left foot and bend a curler for the far corner. Scherpen uses every inch of his towering frame to make an eye-catching diving save.

Maeda shows a great turn of pace to breeze past Mbeumo and reach the byline. Under pressure from Dalot, the winger hits his near post cross into Lammens’ hands.

Again, Rashford runs at Ipswich’s backline and cuts inside to reach the penalty area. He tees up Cunha, who smashes an effort well over the bar.

Martinez attempts an ambitious switch of play, aiming for Maguire, but boots the ball straight out of play. O’Shea and Shaw then both go up for a header, with the Ipswich man coming off worse and staying on the ground. He’s back on his feet now and play resumes.

There’s an early roar from the Old Trafford crowd as Rashford gets on the ball and sprints at Ipswich captain O’Shea, who is playing at right back.

Old Trafford welcomes both sides. Can Man Utd find their first win of the Premier League season or will Ipswich spoil the party?

Carlos Baleba has walking out on to the pitch after being introduced at Old Trafford. The new £70m signing from Brighton has been posing for pictures with a shirt and applauding all sections of the ground. He won’t be in action for another two or three weeks most likely owing to an existing ankle injury.

Carlos Baleba is introduced to the Manchester United fans! 👋 pic.twitter.com/QHTCkpe5dz

Against Hull, Man Utd’s forward line looked way off the pace. In an attempt to stop history repeating itself, Michael Carrick has turned to Marcus Rashford, who is making his first start for the club since the end of 2024.

When Rashford last featured for Man Utd, he was wearing the No.10 shirt. That is now occupied by Mathues Cunha who starts as the central frontman, with Rashford now sporting the No.9.

Is he the man to guide Ipswich to safety?

First game of the season at Old Trafford for United and one they really need to win after last weekend’s shock defeat at newly promoted Hull City.

Summer signing Andrey Santos has made way for Kobbie Mainoo to partner Youri Tielemans in attack and it’ll be really interesting to see how that midfield pairing dovetail.

It’s a first start at Old Trafford since December 2024 for Marcus Rashford in an attacking looking side. Matheus Cunha is likely to operate as a false nine.

There’s going to be an onus on Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo to provide pace and penetration from out wide and get in behind Ipswich’s defence.

Ipswich enjoyed a great start back in the top flight by winning their opening game against Sunderland and will be out to build on that victory.

Against Hull, Michael Carrick opted for a midfield pivot of Man Utd debutants Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. However, the pair were completely overran by Hull’s intensity and energy.

Carrick has turned to Kobbie Mainoo as the resolution, with the 21-year-old replacing Andrey Santos. Mainoo went to the World Cup with England this summer, but didn’t play a single minute.

A return to Old Trafford will give Mainoo a chance to remind everyone of his quality.

📍 Home.Back where we belong. https://t.co/VbvwRcdF4t pic.twitter.com/37rThnGjyN

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

Man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

When the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

Reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick said: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

“So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”

Against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1926. Transfer news: Major Saudi Pro League rule change could shake up the market

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26

With a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads. Saudi Arabia, which has become a leading player in the market in recent years, is considering a change that could boost its domestic league but worry other countries.

According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a new wave of signings. Saudi clubs are seeking clarification on the matter before the Northern Hemisphere winter window in January.

At present, clubs in Saudi Arabia can register up to eight foreign players in a 25-man squad, with the option of adding two more foreign under-21 players for SPL matches. The idea is to raise that limit to 14 or more, with discussions still ongoing.

Should the new rule come into force, Saudi clubs are likely to make more international signings. That could mark a new phase of departures from Europe to join the Saudi project, which aims to improve the competitive level of local football before the country hosts the World Cup in 2034.

In January 2023, Cristiano Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr after terminating his contract with Manchester United, which began a series of Saudi investments in football. In June of that year, the Public Investment Fund (PIF) took control of the four biggest domestic clubs: Al-Ahli, Al-Hilal, Al-Ittihad and Al-Nassr, the Portuguese star's team.

Then Ballon d'Or winner Karim Benzema was another high-profile name to leave Real Madrid for the Saudi Pro League, followed by stars such as N'Golo Kante and Roberto Firmino. Over the past three seasons, Neymar, Ollie Watkins, Gabriel Martinelli, Tijjani Reijnders, Darwin Nunez, Ivan Toney, Sadio Mane and Joao Felix have also been tempted by the Middle East.

As well as drawing global attention to its league, Saudi Arabia believes the move has helped the development of its homegrown talent. Competing for starting places with foreign stars encourages local players to improve.

On the other hand, critics of the proposal to raise the limit on non-Saudi players argue that the rule change could force local players to move abroad, or even leave bigger clubs for smaller ones, in order to get playing time.

It is worth remembering that the PIF has reduced its international sports investments, to the point of ending its backing of LIV Golf. In April, the fund announced a five-year programme with a greater focus on domestic investment. Privatisations of Saudi clubs have also been recurring, such as the sale of 70 per cent of Al-Hilal in August.

Because of the geopolitical context in the region, including Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Yemen-based Houthi rebels, there is some uncertainty over the league's ability to attract foreign players in the short term. In October, the airport in the capital, Riyadh, was hit by a missile attack that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

The Asian Cup, which was due to be held in the country between January and February 2027, was postponed earlier this month. Three SPL matches were also postponed after the October Houthi attacks, although organisers did not attribute the decision to the conflict, saying it was motivated by 'logistical considerations'.

#1924. Arsenal injury news: Mikel Arteta drops update on whether David Raya will be fit to face Man City

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:29

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has refused to confirm whether David Raya will be available for their Premier League showdown with Manchester City on Sunday afternoon.

The Spaniard missed Tuesday night's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League after picking up a shoulder injury against Newcastle United at the weekend.

Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised at the Emirates Stadium, with Arteta offering his backing to the goalkeeper should Raya remain unavailable this weekend.

Raya left the pitch in significant pain during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Magpies on Saturday night, prompting fears that he could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

However, subsequent scans proved positive, with the Spanish goalkeeper avoiding a serious injury and not requiring surgery.

There have been suggestions that Raya could only be sidelined for a matter of days and might therefore be in contention to face City, but Arteta was unwilling to offer any guarantees after the Dortmund draw.

"No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately," the Arsenal manager said (via the Evening Standard). "We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City]."

Arsenal will therefore have to wait for further clarity on their first-choice goalkeeper, with Kepa potentially required to retain his place against Enzo Maresca's side, who also drew at home to Napoli this midweek.

Kepa produced a reasonably solid display in Germany, with Arteta describing his performance as "really good" and insisting that Arsenal fully trust their goalkeepers.

The Spaniard made three saves and received a 7.5 Sofascore rating, making him the Gunners' third-best performer on the night. His expected goals prevented figure of 0.38 also reflected a positive contribution.

There were, however, a few moments that offered cause for concern. Kepa was wrong-footed for Dortmund's goal, while he parried a disallowed effort back into a dangerous area and did not look as assured as Raya when dealing with crosses.

Arteta is nevertheless confident in his deputy, saying: "We fully trust our keepers and if he needs to play against City, he will play."

It is encouraging that Kepa has Arteta's backing, but there would understandably be some apprehension about him starting against a side of City's calibre. Raya's command of his penalty area and reliability have made him an important figure for Arsenal, and his absence would be a significant setback.

However, if the first-choice goalkeeper is not ready, Kepa will have to step up when called upon.

Published: 22:41 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 03:57 EST, 23 November 2026

Inter Miami star Lionel Messi was lucky not to have been sent off after hurling the ball in the face of his opponent during an embarrassing MLS Cup Playoff defeat.

In the Round of 16 contest against the Columbus Crew, Miami went down 1-0 early in the first half with a penalty converted by Gonzalo Tapia. The deficit was then compounded when Miami fullback Gonzalo Lujan was sent off with a second yellow card.

On the stroke of halftime, Messi nearly joined his teammate in the locker room with a moment of madness on a throw-in.

Tapia and Messi were both standing out of bounds as the Chilean striker prevented the World Cup winner from taking his throw right away.

Tapia crumbled to the ground as Messi raised his hands asking for a foul on the Crew star.

Lionel Messi takes a throw-in off Gonzalo Tapia's face pic.twitter.com/jX3tTuojHe

Lionel Messi nearly got sent off during his team's MLS Cup Playoff match against Columbus

A frustrated Messi launched the ball off the face of Crew striker Gonzalo Tapia as he prevented the Argentina star from taking a quick throw in. Both players received yellow cards.

Tapia got revenge by scoring a brace to lead the Crew to a 3-0 victory on Saturday evening

Referee Allen Chapman was not happy with either player's antics, showing yellow cards to both Tapia and Messi.

But ultimately, Columbus and Tapia would get the last laugh as they won 3-0 in the best-of-three Round of 16.

Midfielder Taha Habroune scored the second goal of the evening in the 52nd minute as Tapia secured a brace just six minutes later.

Inter Miami must win the next match in Ohio to stay in the playoffs. If the game finishes tied, the rules dictate the match will proceed directly to penalty kicks.

Out of his three prior seasons in the United States, Messi's 2025 MLS Cup victory was an outlier. Miami missed the playoffs in 2023 and were eliminated in the first round in 2024.

#1922. PSG vs Roma: Luis Enrique issues warning before Roma clash

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:34

Paris Saint-Germain are still coming to terms with the loss of Desire Doue for at least six months because of a serious knee injury, and are making their final preparations to face Roma in the Champions League. One of Luis Enrique's biggest concerns ahead of the game is the red-hot form of Donyell Malen, Roma's top scorer.

At a press conference on Tuesday (24 November), the Spanish manager went out of his way to praise the Dutch forward, who already has 16 goals and four assists in 15 games for Roma this season. Luis Enrique highlighted Malen's improvement since January, when he moved to Italy and developed enormously under Gian Piero Gasperini, forcing Paris Saint-Germain to draw up a special containment plan.

'I am impressed with Donyell Malen and the number of goals he has scored, he has been great this season. Since he started playing as a centre-forward, he has been doing very well. We have to be very careful' - the manager said.

Paris Saint-Germain face Roma on Wednesday (25 November) at 8pm UK time at the Parc des Princes, on matchday five of the league phase. The Spanish boss will try to extend his side's perfect record to stay top of the table, while the Italian manager knows the importance of a surprise result to move towards the knockout phase, as Roma sit 20th with four points.

More than his goalscoring record, the number 14 concerns Luis Enrique because his profile enhances Gasperini's style of play: attacking runs in behind, control of the penalty area and a great ability to finish. Before Malen, Roma suffered from the lack of a player with those characteristics, as neither Artem Dovbyk nor Evan Ferguson had success in the first half of 2025-26.

The solution found by the manager was to use the winter transfer window to take the 27-year-old from Aston Villa, where he had few opportunities as a starter. In England, the Dutchman was used mostly as a winger by Unai Emery, but the Roma boss saw his potential to play in a more central role.

The six-month loan was the turning point for Roma, who climbed from sixth to third in Serie A, securing a return to the Champions League after an eight-year absence. With 14 goals and two assists in 18 league games, Malen was signed permanently from Aston Villa for £23m (€27m).

In 2026-27, thanks to the number 14's fluid partnership with Matias Soule, Paulo Dybala, Wesley, Rodrigo Mora and company, Roma are established in the top four and are Serie A title contenders, sitting second with 30 points, two behind leaders Lazio after 12 matches. Roma have not been Italian champions since 2000-01.

In the best year of his career, the Roma number 14 is the biggest threat to Paris Saint-Germain's defensive system, which knows it cannot afford to slip. Otherwise, Malen is likely to punish the French side with his technical ability and finishing efficiency, even when chances are rare.

#1920. 'The main problem' - Enzo Maresca defends surprise Man City tactical decision after 2-2 Napoli draw

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:48

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has explained some of his unexpected selection and tactical decisions after his side were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday evening.

The result saw City twice come from behind, but their defensive problems continued as they dropped further points in the Champions League.

Maresca also acknowledged that his side are still searching for the right balance between attacking and defending following his arrival as Pep Guardiola's successor.

Maresca left Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye on the bench for the opening hour, while Phil Foden was also rested, prompting questions about his selection.

The City boss explained that his decisions were based on how he expected Napoli to set up, with the visitors having recently used a 3-5-2 or 3-5-1-1 formation.

"We expected Napoli to play 3-5-2 or 3-5-1-1 as they did in recent matches, so that would basically leave eight players in the middle, and hope to create more spaces down the wings," Maresca told Sky Sport Italia.

He wanted Rayan Cherki to operate out wide and exploit those spaces, although City struggled to turn their possession into enough chances during the first half.

Maresca also defended his decision to use Ayyoub Bouaddi in a deeper midfield role alongside Elliott Anderson, explaining that he wanted to maintain balance while allowing six players to attack.

However, the manager admitted that City's defensive shortcomings remain a significant concern.

"The main problem is that we are conceding too many goals, and we need to do something about that," he added.

Maresca also acknowledged that finding the right approach would take time, comparing City's transition to the challenges Arsenal and Manchester United experienced following the departures of Arsene Wenger and Sir Alex Ferguson.

It is not unusual for Maresca to rotate his City side during midweek fixtures, but leaving Doku, Ndiaye and Foden out of the starting lineup for a potentially important Champions League match was still a notable decision.

City ultimately rescued a point, but the draw could prove costly in their hopes of progressing in the competition, particularly given their recent struggles for consistency.

Perhaps Maresca also had this weekend's showdown with Premier League title rivals Arsenal in mind, with City travelling to the Emirates for Sunday's late kick-off.

That is not to suggest the manager deliberately sacrificed the Napoli fixture, but resting Foden and keeping two dangerous wide players in reserve could indicate that he was considering the demands of a huge domestic encounter.

City need to find greater defensive stability regardless of the opposition, as Maresca himself acknowledged, but Sunday's meeting with the Gunners may have been a factor in how he approached his midweek selection.

Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.

Milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth. Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored, in addition to an own-goal that opened the scoring.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was important that the Rossoneri build on their victory over Genoa before the break, especially given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus all won earlier in the round. In addition to that, several individuals shone and the team showed the levels that they are capable of.

Now, the challenge is to follow it up and get back on course in the Europa League in Greece on Thursday night. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to reflect on what was a very positive night for his side, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is that the best Milan performance since you have been here?

“It’s a good feeling, but it’s not just the result: it’s also about consistency throughout the 90 minutes of the match, but now we’re thinking about the next one. It’s always like that at this club, always thinking about the next one.

“Tonight we played well, we were intelligent, courageous, and it showed towards the end of the match. We were tired, yet Frosinone continued to make transitions, but we managed to control them well.

“We could have even scored more goals. Perhaps in the middle of the first half we struggled a little and we need to improve in one-on-one situations defensively, but anyway, it was a good night for us tonight.”

Are you happy for Gonçalo Ramos? How is he?

“We can’t lose any more players. All our players can play every game, but we have little time to recover for the Europa League, so we can’t risk anything. It was better to take him off.

“I imagine he wasn’t happy, but I’m still happy for him, for his goal, especially for the 2-0. It was a goal that made the difference in a match against a team that is very strong in one-on-one transitions.”

Is Rabiot one of the best you’ve ever coached?

“I don’t want to say he could have had a better career because he played at PSG. Now he’s here at Milan and we want him to stay.

“Obviously, he’s a player who can play as a number 10, as an attacking midfielder, he can also play as a number 8, he can also play as a slightly deeper playmaker, even if he doesn’t like it.

“He’s definitely one of the best players I’ve ever coached, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe right now.”

“The first thing I’ll say is that we have to win the match: if we don’t, then it will be really difficult to qualify for the next stage. Then I think that with Rabiot and Pulisic’s characteristics of playing between the lines, when they can’t play, we have to play and approach the game differently.

“But that’s not an excuse. I said the same things against Ferencváros: we should have played a different game and gotten a different result, but what I’m trying to say is that if we don’t win the match, it will be really difficult and things will go badly for us.

“Then, if we exit the Europa League, we’ll only play once a week and many players won’t play enough. However, I think that if we stay in Europe, we can play more and everyone will continue to grow.

“Furthermore, if we don’t qualify, we will fail to achieve an important objective: so that’s why we have to start the match differently than Benfica and Ferencváros. We’ll see.”

What can you tell us about Cisse as a striker?

“I think he can play very well in that role, in that position. Tonight I chose Cissé to play in that position and not Camarda because against Frosinone, one-on-one, Cissé has these characteristics more. Tonight the goal wasn’t to keep possession, but to run and attack the space.

“Cissé is better at this than Camarda. We wanted to make more transitions than Frosinone, so it was a choice dictated by the player’s characteristics, but I think Cissé is good both as an attacking midfielder and as a central striker, and not just as a winger.”
