#1866. Rabiot and Ruben’s rampant Rossoneri: All the key stats from AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone

AC Milan produced their best attacking display of the season on Sunday night as they put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro.

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani early on set the tone, with Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netting in the rout. The ruthless counter-attacking display moves Milan back inside the top four, after wins from Como, Roma and Lazio earlier in the round.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The match stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals – so scoring double what they created – but also having five big chances which matches the number of goals scored.

Frosinone remarkably had more shots in total (15 to 12), but they were more wasteful with only three on target to the Rossoneri’s eight. The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season.

📊 The stats from the win against Frosinone. pic.twitter.com/ERVTj98m9Y

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 22, 2026

Only Nereo Rocco’s (29) and Lajos Czeizler’s (31) Milan sides scored more goals than Ruben Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 matches in charge in Serie A.

Adrien Rabiot is the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal (including goals and assists) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004, and he became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A with more than 10 goals in his first 10 games in a single season.

With his sixth goal in his 10th Serie A appearance for Milan at 20 years and 31 days, Alphadjo Cisse became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato , who achieved it at 18 years and 189 days.

No team has scored more goals than Milan in the first 15 minutes of play in the five major European leagues currently underway (7, like Barcelona and Chelsea).

Milan are now unbeaten in all seven meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W5 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

Milan have won five of their last six league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in a run of Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

Georginio - CF: The striker started at Hull as Charalampos Kostoulas missed training last Friday due to “a personal issue.” Expect Georginio to start this one with Promise David pushing for minutes from the bench.

#1864. Chelsea star Emmanuel Emegha ROBBED by phone snatcher in London after leaving Stamford Bridge following 4-1 hammering by Leeds

Published: 18:28 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:19 EST, 23 November 2026

Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha was robbed after leaving Stamford Bridge on Saturday evening, with the 23-year-old Dutchman having scored in his first start for the club.

Despite grabbing the game's first goal while filling in for the injured Joao Pedro, the Blues were beaten 4-1 by Leeds United and booed both at half-time and full-time.

Daily Mail Sport approached Chelsea and the Metropolitan Police on Sunday morning after hearing that the forward's mobile phone had been stolen after he left the stadium the night before.

Neither stood up the information, but Emegha has now confirmed there was an incident, writing in an Instagram post on Sunday night: 'Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.'

Emegha signed for Chelsea from Strasbourg in the summer on a pre-agreement. The transfer fee between the sister sides has never been disclosed. He has won two caps for the Netherlands national team to date.

An interview with Emegha was included in Saturday's match-day programme in which he said: 'I'm a winner, I'm a fighter. I would do anything to win. If I need to block a ball with the front of my face, I will do it.

Emmanuel Emegha has revealed he was robbed on Saturday after Chelsea's 4-1 loss by Leeds

On Sunday, the Chelsea striker revealed the incident had happened to him on Instagram

He put the Blues ahead at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon - his first goal for the club

'I'm quick, I know how to make runs in behind, and I know that I can be a nightmare for all the defenders. Nobody has seen me yet. When my time comes, I will be ready, and I know that the stadium will love my energy.'

It coincided with him being handed his first start for the Blues and scoring his first goal via a nice left-footed finish. However, Chelsea's 1-0 lead lasted only three minutes as Leeds capitalised on suspect defending to equalise, and then deservedly won.

Noah Okafor scored twice, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson got one goal each.

#1863. Lewes admit: We got what we deserved at Ramsgate

Going into the contest three points ahead of their Kent hosts, Lewes were looking for a result to lift their league form after goalless outings against Enfield Town and Stanway Rovers.

While they did break their goal duck, they were 3-0 down by the time it came in Thanet and went on to lose by a significant margin against their rampant hosts.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

“I think Ramsgate definitely deserved to win,” said Altendorff. “Maybe the scoreline flatters them slightly, but I would say that the end result is justified. We weren't our best.

“Ramsgate were playing a very direct brand of football. We found it difficult to cope with. We didn't win enough first and second contacts, especially in the first half. They got what they deserved, and so did we.”

On a punishing afternoon for the Rooks, heavy first-half pressure led to a fine brace from TJ Jadama, while it could have been worse with another strike rattling the crossbar.

Lewes struggled to escape their half, with Charlie Walker on the end of some contentious decisions as he tried to break away as the sole outlet for much of the match.

While Alfie Allen’s 68th-minute header offered the Rooks some hope, and a quadruple substitution injected some intent, a fourth Ramsgate goal in added time knocked the stuffing out of Lewes.

“The scoreline enabled us to try something different because at that stage of the game, it's already three nil to them,” said Altendorff. “We did actually improve. The boys off the bench did well when they came on.

“I thought Tyler Christian-Law was excellent and added a bit of bite to midfield. We didn't seem to lack anything by withdrawing a third midfielder. If anything, we looked even more threatening.

“Even towards the end of the game, Charlie had a good opportunity to put one in the back of the net from six yards out. Unfortunately, it just wasn't our day. Nothing seemed to fall for us.”

Lewes have now won just one of their last seven Isthmian Premier Division matches and face a tricky test at 7th-placed Leatherhead this Saturday.

Just as Ramsgate were last weekend, the Surrey side are three points behind the Rooks with a game in hand and a superior goal difference, meaning they can leapfrog Lewes with a win.

On Tuesday night, Leatherhead beat Ramsgate 1-0 at home to move into the play-off places, but with this being their first win in four games, the Ian Selley-led side are not in electric form either.
